provenance: LLM-backend-derived + deterministic-checked (Phase 16/17 inverted boundary) — NOT a ship typology config. Previously triaged LOW (the deleted extractor under-counted through this advisory's interleaved footnote runs + page-break running headers). The LLM backend read the source and EXTRACTED the 11 enumerated red flags directly; the deterministic gate GROUNDS each verbatim `flag` in the source md within the red-flag region (normalize() drops the glued 'FINCEN ADVISORY' running header so a header-glued flag still grounds) + checks the cover×data matrix. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo).

indicators.flag: One credit card or bank account is used to book travel to or accommodation and transportation in an area of known ISIS activity for several unrelated people at the same time for no known legitimate purpose.
indicators.red_flag: Shared instrument funding multi-person travel into an ISIS-activity area
indicators.rationale: A single instrument booking travel/accommodation for several unrelated people into an ISIS-activity area is uncovered and computable — the shared card/account, merchant-category (travel), beneficiary count, and destination geo are all in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: one credit card or bank account books travel, accommodation, or transportation into an area of known ISIS activity for several unrelated people within a short window with no known legitimate purpose — a shared instrument funding multi-person travel to a conflict zone
build_logic.source: Core transaction + merchant-category features (Gold); destination-geo / ISIS-area list; beneficiary linkage

indicators.flag: Fundraisers are attached to social media profiles that show support for ISIS or display ISIS-related iconography or refer to supporting the "mujahideen" or the "war against kufar (non-believers)," especially if the fundraisers are soliciting donations to fund travel to an area of known ISIS activity
indicators.red_flag: Crowdfunding via ISIS-iconography social profiles for travel / detainee aid
indicators.rationale: Linking a fundraiser to social-media profiles displaying ISIS iconography or rhetoric is an external open-source signal not held in the AML repo; source that feed before any detection can use it.

indicators.flag: A customer collects small amounts through P2P transfers, social media, or virtual currency payments over a short period of time and then sends them in a lump sum to an individual located in a region where ISIS presence is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: P2P / CVC micro-collection then lump-sum forward to an ISIS-prevalent region
indicators.rationale: Collecting many small inbound P2P/CVC payments then forwarding a lump sum to an individual in an ISIS-prevalent region is uncovered and computable — inbound fan-in, the lump-sum onward transfer, and destination geo are in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a customer collects small amounts through P2P transfers, social media, or virtual currency over a short period and then sends them as a lump sum to an individual located in a region where ISIS presence is prevalent — aggregation-then-forward to a conflict region
build_logic.source: Core transaction + counterparty-geo features (Gold); ISIS-region list

indicators.flag: A customer sends remittances with no known legitimate purpose from the United States to multiple individuals in jurisdictions, such as Türkiye, known for ISIS facilitation activity who do not appear to have any relation to the sender.
indicators.red_flag: Remittance fan-out to unrelated recipients in ISIS-facilitation jurisdictions
indicators.rationale: Remittance fan-out to multiple unrelated individuals in known-facilitation jurisdictions is uncovered and computable — outbound remittance counterparties, their geo, and sender-beneficiary relationship are in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a customer sends remittances with no known legitimate purpose from the United States to multiple individuals in jurisdictions known for ISIS facilitation activity (such as Türkiye) who have no apparent relation to the sender — a fan-out of unrelated remittances to a facilitation corridor
build_logic.source: Core remittance transaction + counterparty-geo features (Gold); facilitation-jurisdiction list; beneficiary linkage

indicators.flag: A customer attempts to purchase plane or other travel tickets after abruptly liquidating assets, closing accounts, cancelling subscriptions, or receiving large unexplained sums of cash
indicators.red_flag: Asset liquidation → travel-ticket purchase → account dormancy
indicators.rationale: Asset-liquidation and account-closure behaviors are partially monitored as mobilization indicators; enhance the existing screen with a liquidation-then-travel-purchase sequence plus a following dormancy window.

indicators.flag: A customer abruptly appears to seek as many lines of credit as possible, for example, by acquiring several credit cards and taking out one or more loans for unclear reasons, especially if the customer has not used credit cards or taken out loans in the past.  This behavior should be regarded as especially suspicious if the customer uses newly obtained credit cards either exclusively or almost exclusively for cash advances and purchases of virtual currencies but then fails to make loan or credit card payments when they come due.
indicators.red_flag: Credit-line burst with no prior history, drawn to cash advances / CVC, then unpaid
indicators.rationale: An abrupt credit-seeking burst by a customer with no credit history, used for cash advances and CVC purchases with no repayment, is an uncovered bust-out-style mobilization pattern, and credit-line openings, advance/CVC usage, and payment status are in repo — immediately buildable.

build_logic.logic: a customer with no prior credit history abruptly opens as many lines of credit as possible (several cards and loans), uses the new credit almost exclusively for cash advances and virtual-currency purchases, then fails to make payments when due — a credit-burst-then-default mobilization pattern
build_logic.source: Core credit-line + transaction features (Gold); repayment/delinquency status

indicators.flag: A customer begins receiving a sudden influx of unexplained cash deposits, especially if that customer is unemployed or these deposits are in addition to a regular paycheck, or if the deposits come from ATMs in locations where ISIS is prevalent, but where the customer is not known to reside or have traveled.
indicators.red_flag: Unexplained cash-deposit influx, including from ISIS-prevalent ATMs off the customer's footprint
indicators.rationale: Unexplained cash-deposit monitoring exists; enhance it with an unemployed-or-beyond-paycheck context plus an ISIS-prevalent ATM-location overlay.

indicators.flag: A customer suddenly adopts or increases their use of financial methods that conceal the ultimate source or end use of funds
indicators.red_flag: Abrupt shift to source-concealing channels (P2P, prepaid, CVC, third-party processors)
indicators.rationale: Channel-shift detection exists; enhance it to flag a sudden adoption/increase of concealment-prone methods (P2P, prepaid, CVC, third-party processors) against the customer's own baseline.

indicators.flag: A customer makes deposits in an account locally which are then withdrawn from other locations, including from abroad, where the individual is not known to reside or have traveled but where ISIS is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: Local deposit / foreign withdrawal divergence into ISIS-prevalent locations
indicators.rationale: Local-deposit / foreign-withdrawal geographic divergence into ISIS-prevalent locations needs withdrawal-location geo plus a customer travel/residence profile we hold only partially; enrich, then build the deposit-vs-withdrawal divergence signal.

indicators.flag: A customer places virtual currency in a virtual currency wallet using an IP address in one location which is then withdrawn from virtual currency kiosks or converted to fiat currency by users with IP addresses in different locations where the individual is not known to reside or have traveled but where ISIS is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: CVC placement-IP vs withdrawal-IP divergence into ISIS-prevalent locations
indicators.rationale: Matching CVC placement-IP against kiosk/conversion withdrawal-IP in ISIS-prevalent locations needs IP-geo on both legs plus kiosk attribution we hold only partially; enrich, then build the IP-divergence signal.

indicators.flag: A customer's account appears to have been accessed in multiple countries at the same time or within a very short time period, particularly if the account is accessed in countries where ISIS is prevalent.
indicators.red_flag: Concurrent multi-country account access, particularly ISIS-prevalent countries
indicators.rationale: Impossible-travel / concurrent-access detection already exists from device-and-session analytics; enhance it with an ISIS-prevalent-country overlay rather than building net-new.
